findings.title: The closed PlanIntent schema admits JSON true and JSON 1.0 where it declares the integer 1, at both commitment-bearing schemaVersion fields
declaredRuleViolated: planIntent.schema.schemaVersion = 1 and planIntent.admissionDescriptorV1.schemaVersion = 1 — integer literals in a schema whose 'closed' flag is true

planIntent.canonicalCommitment.encoding.dataModel — 'JSON objects, arrays, strings, booleans, signed integers and null only; floating-point numbers are forbidden.' Booleans and signed integers are enumerated as DISTINCT types.
planIntent.canonicalCommitment.encoding.closure — 'The PlanIntent schema is closed before encoding, so an unknown field cannot hide outside the commitment.'
planIntent.validationTotality — the declared pre-admission rejection boundary
findings.rootCause: check-c2.py:555 `if intent.get("schemaVersion") != 1` and the corresponding descriptor guard use bare equality. In Python True == 1 and 1.0 == 1, so neither a JSON boolean nor a JSON float is caught. No isinstance check accompanies either comparison.

evidence.boolCase: A wire PlanIntent {"schemaVersion": true, …} is ADMITTED by validate_plan_intent with zero findings, and then commits successfully to a DIFFERENT digest. For valid-minimal-analysis-intent the integer spelling commits to sha256:dca3a310674308c9bb951c5716ee871d19df42f4df07b406533a199d99a8c36d and the boolean spelling to sha256:e86f8120f91c200f5810f9b81393badd2df2fe4478eb74be91e9fe4cc16c1d8b. Mutating the descriptor field instead yields sha256:420beb5968199b146b71d1097891122d277132f992d5973b276bc42c8132de77 and the preimage fragment is literally "schemaVersion":true. The closed schema therefore has two admissible type-distinct spellings of its own version field, each minting its own PlanId.
evidence.floatCase: A wire PlanIntent {"schemaVersion": 1.0, …} is ADMITTED by validate_plan_intent with zero findings, and then canonical_plan_intent RAISES an unguarded ValueError('floating-point values are forbidden'). validate_plan_intent has a totality boundary; canonical_plan_intent and plan_intent_commitment do not.
evidence.reach: 20 admitted-mistyped cases: all 7 valid PlanIntent fixtures, both intentKind branches (analysis and stored-view), both schemaVersion positions. 10 commit to a second digest; 10 admit then raise.
evidence.whyTheAuthorsGeneratorMissedIt: The retained hostile corpus is a 4x4 matrix over four COLLECTION-ADJACENT scalars — resolvedConfiguration[0].path, contribution activationId, contribution contributionId, capabilityGrant grantId — and the checker guards that the matrix stay exactly 4x4. It never injects at a top-level or descriptor-level scalar leaf. schemaVersion is precisely such a leaf. This is the same generator-coverage failure that caused EVIDENCE v9 to be rejected.

findings.reproducibleCondition: Import check-c2.py as a module against the live contract. Take any valid planIntentFixtures[*].intent, set intent['schemaVersion'] = True (or 1.0), call validate_plan_intent(intent, contract, relations). It returns []. For the float, then call plan_intent_commitment(intent, contract): ValueError. Deterministic, no randomness, 20/20 reproducible.
whyBlocking: It is a live, mechanically reproducible violation of the contract's own closure at the field that versions the commitment.

The float case reproduces exactly the failure mode that c2-storage.rereview-reviewer7.json raised as R7R-C2-02 ('the retained PlanIntent validator also raises TypeError for several legal-JSON/wrong-schema nested values rather than returning deterministic pre-admission rejection') and that c2-storage.rereview2-reviewer7.json declared CLOSED-PASS. On the live bytes that property is FALSE at these two fields. A verdict asserting parsed-JSON totality on the live bytes would be inaccurate.
It propagates by direct module import into the evaluation-proof authority join — see downstreamExposure.
The repair is one isinstance guard per site; blocking costs almost nothing and leaves no debt.
findings.requiredRepair: Replace both bare comparisons with an exact-type guard, e.g. `if not isinstance(v, int) or isinstance(v, bool) or v != 1`. Add the analogous guard wherever the contract declares an integer constant or integer range and the checker compares by equality. Add retained selftest mutations that inject boolean and float-equal-to-integer at SCALAR LEAF positions (schemaVersion at both levels, planSchemaMajor, decidingLayer), and extend the guarded totality matrix so it is no longer pinned to exactly 4x4 collection-adjacent keys. Give canonical_plan_intent / plan_intent_commitment the same named-finding boundary validate_plan_intent already has, so that no value the validator admits can raise at the encoder.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A declaration in the live contract that schemaVersion is deliberately type-loose and that boolean/float spellings are intended distinct admissible intents. No such text exists; the dataModel says the opposite.

findings.title: validate_coverage is neither total nor type-checking: it raises on hostile roots and silently conforms falsy relations, bypassing the declared C2X registry check
declaredRuleViolated: coverageKey.key[relation].constraint — 'must exist in fact-plane.v1 relationRegistry', checked: C2X
coverageKey.key[resolution].constraint — 'must be a rung of THAT relation's ladder', checked: C2X

planIntent.validationTotality — the contract's own totality posture, and provider-fact-identity.rereview-reviewer9-response.v1.json#R9-CHECKER-TOTALITY-01, which claims 'each public check()/validate() boundary now has a non-empty object-root guard … and a narrow malformed-shape exception boundary that returns a named finding'

evidence.totalityFailure: 81 hostile node x type mutations of the intra-universe-complete Coverage entry produce 9 EXCEPTIONS: entry = null/0/true/1.5 raise TypeError ('argument of type X is not a container or iterable'); entry = 'str'/[]/['x'] raise AttributeError ('object has no attribute get'); entry.relation = ['x'] or {'x':1} raise TypeError ('unhashable type').
evidence.correctnessHole: relation = null, 0, false, '' , [] or {} — six falsy JSON values — all return ZERO findings. Root cause: `rel = entry.get('relation')` then `if fp and rel:` short-circuits on any falsy value, so the declared C2X registry lookup and the ladder check are both skipped, and `rel in crossUniverseRelations` is False. Contrast relation = 'vibes', which correctly yields "C2X: relation 'vibes' is not in the fact-plane registry". A Coverage entry naming no relation at all is therefore C-2-conformant.
evidence.typeBlindness: sourceUniverseId, targetUniverseId, subjectScopeCommitment, producer, producerVersion and schemaVersion receive NO type or value validation. 58 of 81 mutations return zero findings.

findings.reproducibleCondition: validate_coverage(entry, contract, factplane) with entry['relation'] set to any of None, 0, False, '', [], {} returns []. With entry itself set to None/'x'/[] it raises. Deterministic.
findings.containment: Reached from check() at line 1179, inside check()'s MALFORMED_SHAPE_EXCEPTIONS boundary, so the CLI never tracebacks — my exhaustive 21213-mutation check() fuzz confirms 0 exceptions. The defect is at the public validator, not the CLI.
findings.whyBlocking: The falsy-relation path is not merely a robustness gap; it is a correctness hole in the one C-2 check that the contract labels C2X and that the whole Coverage key exists to enforce. The corpus has already rejected an artifact (D9 v1.13) for shipping a value its checker never validated; this is the same shape.
findings.requiredRepair: Give validate_coverage the same named-finding boundary and non-object-root guard that validate_plan_intent and check() already carry. Replace `if fp and rel:` with an explicit `isinstance(rel, str)` test that emits a C2X finding when relation is not a string. Add per-field type validation for sourceUniverseId, targetUniverseId, producer, producerVersion (strings) and schemaVersion (integer 1), and retained negative fixtures for each.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: Contract text declaring validate_coverage a presence-only helper whose value validation is owned elsewhere. The coverageKey.key constraints say the opposite and name C2X as the checker.

findings.title: subjectScopeCommitment is bound only by key presence; its shipped value violates C-2's own sha256Id wire type and every JSON value is conformant
findings.declaredRuleViolated: coverageKey.key[subjectScopeCommitment] — 'an explicit set commitment over the subjects examined, not an opaque partition label … makes both membership and NON-membership checkable, so we found nothing is distinguishable from we looked at nothing'
evidence: All three valid coverage fixtures ship subjectScopeCommitment = the literal string 'sha256:...'. C-2's own planIntent.wireTypes.sha256Id declares ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$; the shipped value does not match it.
validate_coverage returns zero findings for subjectScopeCommitment set to null, 0, false, '', [], {}, {'a':1}, 'not-a-digest' or the shipped placeholder — 9/9 conformant.
The field has no declared wireType anywhere in C-2.
check-c2.py contains ZERO occurrences of the string 'subjectScopeCommitment'.
findings.relationToPriorFindings: reviewer1's R1-C2-03 recorded the COMPUTATION/VERIFICATION deferral and was adjudicated RESOLVED. knownLimitations repeats it twice. That deferral is honest and I do not reopen it. What is NEW here is that no shape, type or wire grammar is bound either, and that the shipped placeholder contradicts C-2's own sha256Id declaration. Deferring how a commitment is computed does not require leaving its wire type unconstrained.
findings.reproducibleCondition: Set any valid coverage fixture's subjectScopeCommitment to null and call validate_coverage — zero findings.
findings.requiredRepair: Either declare subjectScopeCommitment's wire type in planIntent.wireTypes (sha256Id is the obvious candidate) and enforce it in validate_coverage with a retained negative fixture, or state explicitly in knownLimitations that C-2 binds presence ONLY and that shape is also deferred, so no consumer reads the current text as a shape guarantee. Replace the 'sha256:...' placeholder with a value that satisfies whichever grammar is chosen.
findings.downstreamNote: DELIVERY's R5R-DLTS-03 repair does construct a real reproducible subject-scope commitment, so the product-side gap is smaller than the contract-side gap. The exposure is that C-2, the artifact Evidence joins against, guarantees less than its own prose implies.

findings.title: validate_plan raises TypeError on container-valued stage kind and operator
findings.evidence: 558 hostile mutations across the four valid plan fixtures produce 40 exceptions, all of the form `cannot use 'list'/'dict' as a set element (unhashable type)`, at stages[*].kind (line 267, `kind not in kinds` where kinds is a set) and stages[*].operator. validate_plan is public and its docstring says 'Pure logical stage-plan validation with closed value grammar'.
findings.containment: Both call sites are inside guarded boundaries — validate_plan_intent's try/except (which is why my 5676-mutation PlanIntent fuzz saw 0 exceptions) and check()'s MALFORMED_SHAPE_EXCEPTIONS. No traceback escapes the CLI.
findings.requiredRepair: Guard with `isinstance(kind, str)` / `isinstance(operator, str)` before the membership tests, emitting the same PS-01 finding, and add retained selftest mutations that inject containers at stage kind and operator.

findings.title: planId, snapshotId and executionId are named but ungrammared: no wire type, no live cross-contract join, noncanonical placeholders, and any JSON value validates
evidence: C-2 contains ZERO occurrences of PLAN-ID-V1 or SNAPSHOT-ID-V1. planIntent.wireTypes declares runId, artifactId, factViewId, projectId, sha256Hex, sha256Id, canonicalIdentifier, canonicalRelativePath, boundedParameterValue, semanticVersion, stageBudgetV1 — and no planId, snapshotId or executionId.
C-2's ExecutionPlan/AttemptRecord defaults and fixtures use the noncanonical placeholders 'plan-1', 'snap-1' (x2) and 'exec-1', identically in the contract and the checker.

110 hostile binding mutations produce 20 silent accepts, ALL at executionPlan.planId and attemptRecord.executionId: null, string, integer, boolean, float, list and object are each accepted without a finding.
findings.whyItMatters: This is the same defect class that c2-storage.rereview-reviewer7.json raised as R7R-C2-01 — 'C-2's valid stored-read fixture and checker default use noncanonical request-1 … contradicting live REQUEST-ID-V1' — and that was repaired for RequestId with a byte-exact live join (C2I-OP) and for ProjectId (C2I-TM). The identical defect at planId/snapshotId/executionId was not repaired. The repair standard was applied inconsistently within one contract.
findings.containment: The PlanId RECIPE is bound: planIdentityInputsRequired is an exact 13-field list and the checker rejects shrinking it. PLAN-ID-V1's grammar and derivation are owned by resolved-inputs.v2.json and validated by check-resolved-inputs.py. The gap is that C-2's own ExecutionPlan envelope contract constrains none of the three identifier VALUES it carries.
findings.requiredRepair: Add planId / snapshotId / executionId wire types to planIntent.wireTypes joined byte-exactly to resolved-inputs.v2.json (the C2I-OP pattern), enforce them in validate_intent_binding, replace 'plan-1'/'snap-1'/'exec-1' with canonical values, and retain negative fixtures.

verdictStatement.scope: architecture/design integrity of the LIVE C-2 bytes 3c488ff6… with checker 4f31d57c…, at IMPLEMENTABLE_UNEXECUTED / SPECIFIED assurance
verdictStatement.basis: The live bytes are strong in every place I could test them against their own declarations: closure is genuinely mechanical (288/288 malformed and 78/78 well-formed unknown-key injections rejected at every closed record node); every enum, ordering, range, path, digest, semver and bounded-parameter rule I could name from the contract text is enforced (30/33 declared-constraint cases conform); the REQUEST-ID-V1 stored-read join is exact and byte-joined to the live OPERABILITY artifact (113/113 cases, zero accepts, zero exceptions); check() is total over 21213 exhaustive hostile mutations of its own 2357-node contract; --selftest is live and load-bearing; and planIntentCommitment reproduces 7/7 first attempt from two independently written encoders, plus both downstream evaluation-proof vectors including EP8's exact 2463-byte preimage length. That is a genuinely good artifact. It is nevertheless a REJECT, on two grounds. First, LB-C2-01: the schema declared 'closed' admits JSON true and JSON 1.0 at the integer schemaVersion field, in both branches of both positions across all seven valid fixtures — the boolean minting a second admissible commitment and the float admitting then raising an unguarded ValueError at the encoder. That float case is the exact failure mode a prior independent review raised as R7R-C2-02 and a later one declared CLOSED-PASS; on these bytes it is open, and it is open specifically in the scalar-leaf region the author's own 4x4 hostile matrix is pinned never to reach. Second, LB-C2-02: validate_coverage raises on seven hostile roots and silently conforms six falsy relation values, so the C2X fact-plane-registry check the Coverage key exists to enforce is bypassed by a null. Both are small, mechanical repairs. Neither can be waived without making a false statement about parsed-JSON totality or about C2X.
verdictStatement.whatThisVerdictIsNot: This is not product qualification, not demonstration, not release approval, not an architecture seal, and not an integration decision. It renders the missing independent verdict on the live C-2 bytes and nothing more.

residuals.title: The commitment grammar's disputable clauses have no discriminating vector
residuals.detail: Across all seven valid PlanIntent fixtures the committed data contains zero non-ASCII keys, zero non-ASCII strings, zero control characters, zero characters requiring a JSON escape, zero negative integers and zero integers above 2^53. Exactly one string contains a solidus ('src/lib.rs'), which does usefully exercise the 'solidus is not escaped' clause. The clauses on NFC normalisation, lowercase shortest-required escapes, ascending Unicode scalar-value key order (as opposed to UTF-16 code-unit order), and 'no leading plus' are therefore untested by any retained vector. Two independent implementers agreeing 7/7 is weaker evidence than it appears, because the exercised subset is the trivially unambiguous one. Recommend adding at least one valid vector carrying a decomposed-vs-composed Unicode string, an astral-plane key, an escape-requiring character and a negative integer.

residuals.title: check() does not validate the contract's own prose and metadata fields
residuals.detail: Of 21213 exhaustive check() mutations, 8220 leave the checker reporting clean. Sampling shows these are overwhelmingly narrative fields — artifact, version, supersedes, purpose, status, why, note, v2Defect and similar. This is arguably correct for a contract checker, but it means the artifact's self-description (including the two-edits-stale status prose noted in LB-C2-06) is entirely unguarded, and $.version could be set to null without any checker objecting.

residuals.title: Fixtures and validator still share one author
residuals.detail: The live knownLimitations says so explicitly. My independent encoder and probes reduce this exposure for the commitment and for closure/totality, but not for the semantic correctness of the fixture corpus itself.

residuals.title: PS-07, PS-09 and PS-12c remain implementable:false
residuals.detail: Three of twenty-two conformance tests are unbuilt; the CONDITIONAL and PARTIAL discharge states are correct honesty, C3X mechanically refuses paper seals, and reviewer1's R1-C2-01 already adjudicated this. My Segment A reconstruction is therefore inferential — sound, corroborated by four independent artifacts and by the mutation-count and commitment-digest trails, but it is inference, not the bytes.
